concepts.def: A diagram showing the energy of reactants and products and the activation energy.
Endothermic — energy must be supplied to break chemical bonds.
Exothermic — energy is released when new bonds form.
Whether a reaction is exothermic or endothermic overall, found by comparing energy to break and make bonds.
How much product is formed; reversible reactions reach a balance that limits yield.
Conditions chosen to balance a good rate, a reasonable yield and cost.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Steepest gradient = fastest rate.

Curve flattens when reactant runs out.

Total amount produced is the final y-value.

Exothermic: products lower than reactants. Endothermic: products higher.

Activation energy = peak height above reactants.

Catalyst lowers the peak but does not change enthalpy.

Always a compromise between rate, yield and cost.

Higher temperature: faster but lower yield (if exothermic forward).

Catalyst: cheaper - higher rate without high temperature.

mcqs.q: On a reaction profile, activation energy is shown by:
A catalyst affects which of these?
How does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
options: Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
It provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.
A catalyst lowers the activation energy of the original reaction pathway.

mcqs.q: In an exothermic reaction, what happens energetically with the bonds?
options: The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
Bond breaking releases energy and bond making absorbs energy.
Energy released forming new bonds exceeds energy absorbed breaking existing bonds.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.

mcqs.q: When water boils, what is broken?
options: Water molecules split into hydrogen and oxygen gas when they boil.
The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.
Intermolecular forces (hydrogen bonds) between water molecules are broken — the O-H covalent bonds stay intact.
The covalent bonds between hydrogen and oxygen atoms are broken when water boils.
